home.description: Plausible job roles for a digital health care organisation: titles, bands, responsibilities, skills, and job evaluation scores, aligned with the UK GDaD PCF and ESCO, for self assessment, performance review, and skills gap analysis.
home.heading: Roles and skills for digital health care
home.lede: Plausible job roles for a digital health care organisation, from service desk to director. Each role level has a title, a band, responsibilities, skills with expected levels, and job evaluation scores, aligned with the UK Government Digital and Data Profession Capability Framework and ESCO.
home.find_html: Search every role level, or browse by family or band. Pick the closest match: many jobs mix two roles.
home.assess_text: Every role level page has a self assessment. Rate yourself against each skill, add evidence, and see your gaps. Your answers stay in your own browser, and you can download them as a spreadsheet file to take to your manager.
home.review_text: Each role level sets out what the role expects at that band: responsibilities, skills and their levels, and a short band outline. Use it as a shared starting point for development conversations.
home.gap_html: Download each person's completed self assessment and combine them with the gap analysis script in the repository, to see a team's strengths and gaps skill by skill.
home.band_heading: See why a role sits in its band
home.band_html: Every role level is scored on 16 job evaluation factors, such as knowledge, freedom to act, and mental effort. The total places it in its band. The scores are illustrative, not a formal evaluation.

jes.description: The 16-factor job evaluation scheme: factors, levels, points, and band points ranges.
jes.lede: Every role level is scored on 16 factors. Each factor has numbered levels worth a set number of points, and the total places the role level in its band.
jes.warning: The scores in this reference are illustrative. They show why a role level sits in its band. A real evaluation scores the actual job, from an agreed job description, by a trained panel.
jes.principle_1: Score the job, not the person doing it.
jes.principle_2: Score the normal, regular requirements of the job, not rare events.
jes.principle_3: Score the minimum knowledge needed to do the job, gained by any route.
jes.principle_4: Choose the level whose summary best fits the job as a whole.

about.description: What this reference is, how it was built, the frameworks it uses, and its licences.
about.heading: About this reference
about.lede: An open reference of plausible job roles for a generic digital health care organisation, for skills gap analysis, performance review, and self assessment.
about.disclaimer: These are illustrative reference profiles for a generic digital health care organisation. They are not official job descriptions for any employer, and their job evaluation scores are not a formal evaluation. Where your actual job description, objectives, or evaluated job differ, those take priority.
about.pcf_heading: UK Government Digital and Data Profession Capability Framework
about.pcf_html: The UK GDaD PCF describes 53 digital and data roles, 206 role levels, and 186 skills, each skill on four levels. Where one of its roles fits, this reference uses it as the base, quotes its role and level descriptions and skills word for word, and uses its Civil Service grades to suggest bands. Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0. © Crown copyright.
about.esco_html: ESCO, the European Skills, Competences, Qualifications and Occupations classification, describes 3,039 occupations and 13,939 skills and knowledge concepts in 28 languages. Every role here links to ESCO occupations, with their essential and optional skills, and every skill links to its closest ESCO skills. Contains ESCO v1.2.1 data. © European Union. Reuse authorised under Commission Decision 2011/833/EU.
about.isco_html: The International Standard Classification of Occupations (ISCO-08) is a four-level hierarchical framework managed by the International Labour Organization (ILO) to categorise jobs around the world by skill level and specialisation. Every ESCO occupation sits within an ISCO-08 group, and each role here shows the ISCO-08 codes of its ESCO occupations.
about.sfia_html: The Skills Framework for the Information Age (SFIA) is a global model that defines digital, information technology (IT), and software-related skills, competency levels, and role profiles. Each band here records its typical SFIA level of responsibility. SFIA levels are named only; SFIA text is not reproduced.

about.built_html: The data lives as YAML in the repository, where a build script validates every role level, including that its job evaluation total falls within its band, and generates this site's data. Editors can change the data in a browser through the content manager, which commits to the repository. This site is prerendered with SvelteKit and built with the Lily Design System™.
